$comment: The CROSS-LANGUAGE conformance vector for the #508 per-request credential's signed payload.
Contract: signed_payload = framed(CONTEXT) | framed(ticket) | framed(rpc_full_name) |
framed(resource_id) | framed(body_digest), where framed(x) = u32_little_endian(len_bytes(x)) | x,
CONTEXT is the ASCII bytes of `domain` below, ticket is RAW BYTES, and the three remaining fields
are UTF-8 encoded. The client signs those bytes with the agent's Ed25519 key and sends the
signature as x-seam-call-sig (base64) on HTTP / x-seam-call-sig-bin on gRPC.
`rpc_full_name` is the gRPC full method path on BOTH transports, never the HTTP route pattern.
That is what makes ONE credential valid over either plane for a bodyless verb.
For a BODIED verb the credential is per-transport and cannot be reused across planes: HTTP frames
JSON and binds the path id plus a digest of the exact request bytes; gRPC frames protobuf, leaves
resource_id EMPTY, and digests the whole request message (the id is inside it). See the two
bodied-verb cases.
Every SDK and framework adapter MUST reproduce `payload_b64` byte-for-byte from the inputs.
The Rust reference is crates/seam-api/tests/request_sig_payload_vector.rs; the RUNTIME's own
seamd::authorize::request_sig_payload is asserted against this same file by
crates/seamd/tests/request_sig_payload_conformance.rs, so the spec and the server cannot drift.
There is deliberately NO bless mode. `seam-request-call-v1` is a frozen signed-wire construction:
a mismatch is a CONTRACT BREAK, not a prompt to regenerate. Changing these bytes costs a v2 domain

Bytes are lowercase HEX, matching seam-sdk's sibling conformance/call_sig_payload_vector.json for the seam-authorize-call-v2 framing. An SDK author implements both in one sitting; two encodings across two vectors of the same shape is a transcription bug waiting to happen.
tag, a second vector and an SDK migration. To ADD a case, run the reference test with
SEAM_PRINT_REQUEST_SIG_VECTOR=1 and paste what it prints.

A case marked `synthetic: true` uses a method name that is NOT a real RPC. Those rows exist to pin the framing itself (length prefixing, the all-empty degenerate), not any verb's contract, and the runtime-side test skips them when it checks that every other row names a genuinely credentialed verb.
framing: u32-LE length prefix per field, five fields in order: domain, ticket, rpc_full_name, resource_id, body_digest

cases.name: bodyless-read
cases.why: the shape the canary's read-back leg sends: a GET with no body, so body_digest is the empty string and the payload is byte-identical over HTTP and gRPC

cases.name: same-ticket-and-resource-different-verb
cases.why: THE re-pointing guard. Identical ticket and decision_id as the case above, only the verb differs — GetCommitmentProof returns the DECRYPTED commitment where GetDecision returns structural columns. An implementation that omits rpc_full_name produces the same bytes for both and is exploitable, not merely non-conformant

cases.name: bodied-verb-http
cases.why: HTTP frames JSON, so a bodied verb binds the path id AND a digest of the exact request bytes. Re-serializing before digesting (key reordering, whitespace) produces a different digest and fails to authenticate

cases.name: bodied-verb-grpc-whole-message
cases.why: gRPC frames protobuf, and the resource id lives INSIDE the message — so the resource_id slot is the EMPTY string and the digest covers the whole decoded request frame, binding strictly more. The consequence a client must know: for a BODIED verb the credential is per-transport; only the bodyless reads are portable

cases.name: length-prefix-disambiguation-a
cases.why: paired with -b. Without the u32-LE length prefixes these two concatenate identically, re-opening exactly the verb/resource re-pointing gap the framing exists to close. The two payloads below MUST differ

cases.name: length-prefix-disambiguation-b
cases.why: see -a. Same concatenated characters, different field boundaries

cases.name: all-fields-empty
cases.why: the degenerate row. Five zero u32 prefixes after the context field — an implementation that skips empty fields rather than length-prefixing them diverges here and nowhere else

cases.name: multibyte-resource-id
cases.why: lengths are BYTES, not characters. A UTF-16 or code-point length (JavaScript's .length, Python's len on str) produces a shorter prefix and an unverifiable signature

cases.name: binary-ticket-with-nul-and-high-bytes
cases.why: the ticket is RAW BYTES, never a string. A client that decodes it to UTF-8, or truncates at a NUL, signs something else. Base64 in this fixture is transport for the vector file only
